concepts.name: Serving size
concepts.source_span: The numbers on a label are given for one serving, or for a fixed amount such as 100 grams. - A pack often contains more than one serving, so eating the whole pack means multiplying the numbers. - Always check the serving size and the number of servings per pack before comparing products.

questions.stem: A pack contains 3 servings and one serving has 200 kcal. How many kcal are in the whole pack?
What should you check before comparing two products?
options: The serving size and servings per pack

questions.stem: The numbers on a label are usually given for:
options: One serving or a fixed amount such as 100 grams

questions.stem: Why can the whole pack have more calories than the main numbers suggest?
options: The pack may hold more than one serving
The numbers are for the packaging

questions.stem: If you eat two servings, you should:
options: Double the numbers on the label

questions.stem: How are calories written on a label?
What is another unit of energy on labels?
About how many kilojoules equal one kilocalorie?
What do calories tell you?
options: How much energy the food gives you

questions.stem: Do calories show whether a food is healthy?
options: No, they only show the amount of energy

concepts.name: Macronutrients
concepts.source_span: Fat gives 9 kcal per gram, more than double the other two.

questions.stem: Which macronutrient gives 9 kcal per gram?

How much energy do carbohydrates give per gram?

What is fibre?
options: A carbohydrate the body cannot fully digest

concepts.name: Sugars
concepts.source_span: Added sugars are sugars put in during making, such as in biscuits and soft drinks.

concepts.source_span: To convert sodium to salt, multiply the sodium amount by 2.5.

concepts.name: Ingredients and daily value
concepts.source_span: Ingredients are listed in order of weight, with the heaviest ingredient first.
